Anyways - I recommend a small study of gold geology through the winter months. Gold is often found in rivers, and in former river beds. Before the last ice age the rivers were located in different areas. The gold deposited by these former rivers is still in the ground, usually untouched by human hands. Geology can help you find them.

These days, most of the existing rivers have been explored over the past two hundred years or so. Finding fresh untapped deposits is often not so easy. Still, even looking at old gold bearing areas is sometimes the best ways to find new gold deposits. Where gold is found, often more gold is found.

Gold is produced as a byproduct of the volcanic forces of the Earth, and is often found where mountains are being pushed up, near volcanoes, and along geological fault lines. So usually the best river gold is found where rivers run across mountains and fault lines upstream.

Anywhere in the Rocky Mountains, or the Canadian Shield, or really any fault line, all of these areas have improved chances for finding gold.

Ancient rivers that used to cross these areas are known to have carried large deposits well downstream.
